The grant

What does the grant cover?

Erasmus+ uses fixed amounts per participant, per day or per distance. Your school shows the activity happened, not every receipt.

Travel

A fixed amount based on the distance band between your town and the destination. Green travel (train, bus, car-sharing) receives a higher amount.

Individual support

A daily amount for accommodation and living costs. It depends on the destination country.

Course fees

For structured courses: an amount per participant per day of the course, up to a maximum per participant.

Organisational support

A fixed amount per participant for the school's work: preparation, follow-up and sharing results.

Inclusion support

Extra funding for participants with fewer opportunities or special needs.

Not covered

Private extensions of the trip, extra holiday days and personal expenses that are not part of the learning activity.

Amounts change every year: check the current Erasmus+ Programme Guide and your National Agency.

The Erasmus+ year

From idea to classroom in five steps

Prepare · Sep – Jan. Agree the needs of your school, choose the teachers and pick courses that answer those needs.

Apply · February. The main KA121 and KA122 deadline is usually in February. Some countries open a second KA122 round in the autumn.

Results · May – Jul. Your National Agency publishes the results and the school signs the grant agreement.

Go · Summer. Five days of training abroad with teachers from all over Europe.

Share · Back home. Try what you learned with your class, share it with colleagues and write the final report.

Dates change every year and country: always check your National Agency.

True or false?

Test yourself in 30 seconds

  1. The teacher applies for the grant personally.

    False: the school (or a consortium) applies to its National Agency.

  2. Travelling by train can bring a higher travel grant.

    True: green travel receives a higher amount.

  3. A school needs an accreditation for its first project.

    False: KA122 is made for schools without an accreditation.

Erasmus+ explained

Everything you need to know, in plain words

Erasmus+ for teachers: the 5-minute guide

Erasmus+ is the European Union's programme for education, training, youth and sport. For teachers it does one thing extremely well: it pays for professional learning abroad.

What a teacher can do with Erasmus+

  • Courses and training: a structured course with teachers from other countries, from 2 to 30 days.
  • Job shadowing: observe colleagues in a school or organisation abroad, from 2 to 60 days.
  • Teaching assignments: teach in a partner school abroad, from 2 to 365 days.

Who applies

The school applies, not the individual teacher. It sends its application to the National Agency of its country. Schools without experience can also join a consortium, often coordinated by a regional or local education authority.

What the grant covers

The grant is calculated with fixed amounts (unit costs): travel according to distance, daily support for accommodation and living costs, course fees for structured courses, and organisational support for the school. Participants with fewer opportunities can receive extra support.

Where to start

Talk to your head teacher or international coordinator. Find out whether your school has an Erasmus accreditation or has ever run a project. If not, the short-term route (KA122) is the usual first step.

Next: open The routes to see the three doors in detail.

KA122, KA121 or accreditation? Choosing your school's route

Every school that wants Erasmus+ mobility uses one of three doors. The right one depends on your experience and on how many mobilities you plan.

KA122: short-term projects

Designed for schools without an Erasmus accreditation. A project lasts between 6 and 18 months and can include up to 30 participants. It is the natural first project for a school that is new to Erasmus+.

KA120 accreditation, then KA121 every year

An accreditation is a long-term commitment: the school writes an Erasmus Plan with objectives for several years. Once accredited, it requests a budget every year through KA121, without writing a full project each time.

Consortium

A coordinator (often a regional or local education authority) holds an accreditation and organises mobilities for a group of schools. It is a good option for small schools with little time to manage a project.

How to decide

  • Never applied before? Start with KA122.
  • Planning mobilities every year for several years? Consider accreditation.
  • Small school, little capacity? Ask about a consortium.

Deadlines

The main deadline for KA121 and KA122 is usually in February. Some countries open a second KA122 round in the autumn. Accreditation applications are usually due in the autumn. Dates change every year, so always check your National Agency.

What does an Erasmus+ grant cover?

Erasmus+ mostly uses unit costs: fixed amounts per participant, per day or per distance. Your school does not need to justify every receipt; it needs to show that the activity took place.

The budget items

  • Travel: a fixed amount based on the distance band between your town and the destination. Green travel (train, bus, car-sharing) receives a higher amount.
  • Individual support: a daily amount for accommodation and living costs. It depends on the destination country.
  • Course fees: for structured courses, an amount per participant per day of the course, up to a maximum per participant.
  • Organisational support: a fixed amount per participant for the school's work: preparation, follow-up and sharing results.
  • Inclusion support: extra funding for participants with fewer opportunities or special needs.

What it does not cover

Private extensions of the trip, extra holiday days and personal expenses that are not part of the learning activity.

A practical tip

Prepare your budget with the current Programme Guide and your National Agency's tables: amounts are updated every year.

How to choose a course abroad that your evaluator will love

Evaluators do not fund destinations. They fund answers to your school's needs. Use these five questions to choose a course.

1. Does it answer a real need?

Start from your school's development plan. If your need is student wellbeing, a wellbeing course is easier to justify than a general one.

2. Are the learning outcomes clear?

Look for a course programme with concrete outcomes you can quote in your application.

3. Will you meet teachers from other countries?

Small international groups give you new ideas and future partners for eTwinning or KA2 projects.

4. Do you receive a certificate?

Ask for a certificate of attendance with the hours and the content. It helps your final report and your Europass Mobility.

5. Can you share it when you come back?

The best courses give you activities you can try with colleagues the week you return.

Frequently asked questions

Is it really free?

Yes. The microcourse, the resources and the certificate are free. You only need an approved account.

Who can join?

Teachers, coordinators, school leaders and teacher trainers from any European country.

Can my school pay an eMove course with Erasmus+?

Yes. eMove courses are structured courses designed for Erasmus+ KA1 projects, so the grant can cover the course fee, travel and daily costs.

What language is the platform in?

The platform is in English, the common language of eMove courses.

How long does approval take?

We review requests by hand, usually within a few days. You can check the status by signing in.

Who is responsible

EMOVE Profe is run by eMove Academy (Barcelona, Spain). Contact: emovecourses@gmail.com.

What we collect

Why we use it

  • To review your request and manage your access.

  • To understand how the platform is used and improve it.
  • Only if you tick the box: to send you news about Erasmus+ deadlines and eMove courses. You can change this in your profile at any time.

Where it is stored

Your account is stored with our hosting provider (Netlify). Your browser also keeps a local copy of your progress so the platform works offline. We do not use advertising or tracking cookies; this website only remembers the language you choose in your browser.

How long we keep it

While your account is active. Ask us to delete your account at any time and we will erase your details and progress.

Your rights

You can ask to access, correct or delete your data, or object to its use, by writing to emovecourses@gmail.com. You can also complain to your data protection authority.
